page.layout: Running head top centre and page number top left. Two woodcut medallion portraits centred at the top, with their legends around them (left: EVDOCIA; right: DIOGENES ROMANVS). Below them, one column of running text in two paragraphs. No margin notes, no notes under the text.

main_text.l: EVDOCIA
DIOGENES ROMANVS
EVDOCIA cum filiis imperat Constantinopoli post
Constantinum Ducam,anno mundi 5031. à Christo nato 1069.
Poterat muliebri fortasse prudentia hęc,si foris cessassent bella,
imperiũ domi administrare: sed lacessentibus undique impe-
rium barbaris,vicit eorum sententia,qui rebus præficiendũ vi-
rum appositum ac idoneum contendebāt. Quare iurisiurandi
oblita,quo marito Ducæ,morieti, se obstrinxerat, non superin-
ducturam se virum, etiam si coacta esset, Romanū cognomine
Diogenem,post menses imperij septem,in virum Eudocia assu-
mit, qui republ. prudentia ac fortitudine tueretur: at pœnituit
statim Eudociam,quòd vir hic insolens rem ad se totam trahe-
ret. Vide Egna. lib.2.Cosmog. Mun.lib.4.
ROMANVS Diogenes Eudociæ vir,imperat Constanti-
nopoli, anno mundi 5032. à Christo nato 1070. duas hic su-
scepit expeditiones vario rerum successu : prior quidē optimè
cessit,posteriorautem pessimè:nam vel fugatis vel cæsis militi-
bus suis ipse Imperator Constantinopolitanus capitur:quod ad
eam diem nunquã contigerat. Ferunt tamen Turcam nomine
Azan,ad primũ huius euentus nuncium, vix credentem consti-
tisse:mox ad se adductum Ro.Diogenem, & cognitū, in precio
habuisse: ac amplis donatum muneribus, pace inita, dimisisse.
Sed ad primum aduersæ cladis nuncium, ut ferè fit, omnia Co-
nstantinopoli iam mutata erat:Eudocia nempe relegata est:Ro-
mano abdicatum est imperium : Michaël Imperator creatus,
Romanum Diogenē victum, deditúmque , contra iusiurandũ
exoculat, ac in insulam deportat, ubi ab uxore Eudocia sepe-
litur, post annos imperij ferè quotuor. Vide ut supra.

page.notes: Printed "morieti" read as shown; uncertain of the vowel. "quotuor" is as printed (apparent printing error for quatuor). Figures 5031, 5032, 1069, 1070 are in old-style form and read as shown. Medallion legends are printed on the woodcuts and are given as lines above the text.
